_comment: The hike -> photograph join, confirmed row by row. Every row rests on NYNJTC's OWN pairing rather than on a score: `basis` was `page + title`, meaning the archived write-up whose title is character-for-character this hike's name displayed this photograph in its markup. `credit` is read from that same page's img, which is the wording sources.json's nynjtc_hikes_licence makes a condition - 'the credit line the page carries'. Confirmed against run 35202093452's sheet (2026-09-17), taken over the full recovery of 439 of 444 write-ups: of its 356 credited proposals, the 46 placed by a NEARBY rather than an identical title, the 8 carried by subject-text scoring alone, the 1 whose hike the export could not place, and 9 whose page title did not match character-for-character are deliberately NOT here and remain for a person to work through - as do the 182 the sheet flags as page-versus-words disagreements. One photograph per hike, because a card shows one. Removing a row stops that photograph shipping AND stops its bytes reaching the bucket, because publish.py reads the same digests.
